lines.text: Each tire has one grip budget. Picture it as a circle.
Driving forward uses some. Spinning the robot uses some too. They add like the sides of a right triangle, so spinning up costs a little forward push.
When the two together are too much, we shrink both by the same amount. That way the robot keeps heading the same direction, just a little slower.
And quick changes in spin are the worst: in our simulator, most wheel slip came from turning, not driving. So spin may only change by eight radians per second squared.
